title: Linear independence of 1, zeta(2), and zeta(3)
abstract: Proves that 1, the Riemann zeta function at 2, and its value at 3 are linearly independent over the rationals, using integer polynomial approximation, p-adic coefficient bounds, prime-edge nonvanishing, and logarithmic potential energy estimates for Hankel determinants. Includes reusable irrationality criteria, contour integration, Andreief identities, Newton-basis valuation bounds, and energy inequalities for finite measures. The cited source is the completed Lean proof; independent novelty of the informal argument is not claimed.

informal.Zeta32.one_zeta_two_zeta_three_linearInd: The three complex numbers 1, riemannZeta 2, and riemannZeta 3 are linearly independent over the rational numbers.
informal.Zeta32Acceptance.one_zeta_two_zeta_three: For rational a, b, and c, if a plus b times the real sum of 1/(k+1)^2 plus c times the real sum of 1/(k+1)^3 is zero, then all three coefficients are zero; both sums range over natural numbers k.
informal.Zeta32.zeta3_sub_rat_mul_zeta2_irrationa: For every rational r, the real series for zeta(3) minus r times the real series for zeta(2) is irrational.
